chapter: Wes's death and Monk's turning point
title: Wes's last engagement and death; Monk stops playing for months
summary: Monk stopped playing for months afterward; after a final Phoenix engagement Wes phoned twice that week, and a sister called Saturday with the news.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Did you stop playing after he died? I read that somewhere.
Yeah, I did, for a period.
It went into months, I don't know how many. Four or five, maybe. Just wild guesses, but it was just a few months.
And then how did you start again?

It was kind of strange. Let me just wind up this one part about Wes because our last and final engagement as it would happen. During that week that we were off, we went to start back to work...Our last date working was in Phoenix, Arizona. We played three nights down there at a place called Caesar's something; the guy was called Caesar. That was our last engagement. We were off for one week and we were to start back on these concerts. We had just ended the nightclubs and...

...going into the next phase. We had a week off. I came home, went to Los Angeles; Buddy went to San Francisco. And it was a thing like, even when we were off, we'd talk to each other every day or so. We were very close.

And he called me on a Tuesday, and we were just talking, just talking. And I was looking forward to going back. And we had a whole week off. I hear from Wes all the time; you know, we'd call back and forth, like that, but I thought it was unusual to keep talking so long. We had just finished that Saturday night and it was like Tuesday. Maybe there was something to talk about in between, but not that long. We were

And then he was saying things like, 'Is everything all right?' And I would say, 'Yeah, everything is great.' That was his way of asking, do you need anything. And he would speak to my wife, and it was sort of like hanging on to the phone. I didn't pay it too much attention, but then he called me Thursday. Two days later he called me again. And we talked for a long time, so he was telling me about that he had gone to the doctor and they had him in...He was a chain smoker, and he was smoking these cigarettes was made out of lettuce. Just couldn't give up the cigarette thing, right? And he had to give up meat. And he had to give up salt and he was taking some pills and so-and-so. I knew he was nervous about his condition, I knew that.

And we talked so long on Thursday. And Saturday morning, early Saturday morning, I got a call from my sister. And when I answered the phone she said, 'Monk, Wes is dead.' And that about...I never experienced a shock that I had that morning. Just simple and to the point, she said it. Then I began to put all those other pieces together. And then, naturally, all of that was explained to us by his doctor, afterwards, his real condition. They kept it from us but they told his wife more than they told us, and she kept it from us.

The doctor knew, the last time Wes had visited him, that he couldn't go back to playing. He knew he wasn't strong. He knew it was over but he couldn't tell Wes. So he told Wes to take off three weeks, and then we'd talk about it. And most of the things he was telling me, that the doctor wanted him to stay off for three weeks. He said, 'Man, I can't do it. We got these things coming up and so-and-so...' I said, 'Just take it easy, man, I'll carry your guitars to the airports and things.'

You know, his wind was short and he couldn't do this. 'No problem, man, you're living like a king now, you're flying everywhere and the best hotels. You just play a little bit at night, you cut that back. We'll...Let the band play more. We don't have to rehearse. We'll do a whole lot of things, right?'

But he was living in that fear to the point of not knowing the extent of how bad it was. But the doctor told us afterwards it was over. His heart was just, the condition of it...His playing days was over then.
Was that something he had had all his life and nobody knew? Rheumatoid arthritis or one of those things that you don't...

Don't know, didn't any of us to my knowledge. I know I didn't. I didn't dig it up, or stir it up, or try to do a 'roots' thing on his health. That was it. Wes was gone. He was gone and that was it. And that's when...
